editorial: We didn't keep a clean expense ledger, but Iceland was unmistakably one of the pricier destinations on our travels.
The expensive parts are structural: car rental, fuel, accommodation and eating out. Unlike a city break, there are fewer clever substitutions because the road trip itself is the product.

alternatives.title: What if we had a bigger budget?
editorial: We'd spend it on extra nights and better-located stays along the route, not luxury for luxury's sake. Time and flexibility are the most valuable upgrades in Iceland.

alternatives.title: What if we had a smaller budget?
editorial: Travel with people you like enough to share a car and rooms with, buy groceries where practical and resist adding paid experiences to every day. The waterfalls, glaciers and beaches are already doing the heavy lifting.

title: What it's Going to Cost
